transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I’m convinced some labs are secretly using people like my mom and our community in dangerous experiments, and no one can show me anything that truly proves otherwise. I decided to come here because my family keeps telling me I'm wrong, but I know what is happening.
How long have you felt this way, and have these specific beliefs about the experiments been present for at least six months?

Yes, I've been dealing with this for about a year now, so it has definitely been much longer than six months. It all started around the time my mother's diabetes complications got worse and I began accompanying her to all her specialist appointments. That's when I first started noticing what was really going on with the labs and how they were targeting our community.

Besides these specific beliefs, have you noticed a decline in your ability to handle daily tasks like work or personal hygiene, or have you experienced symptoms like feeling emotionally flat or having difficulty speaking?

My daily hygiene and work performance are completely fine—I still show up for my shifts, draw blood, and handle all my routine tasks successfully, though my supervisor thinks I'm just intense. My relationships with my family and certain coworkers are definitely strained because I'm trying to warn them and protect my mother, but I absolutely don't have any issues like feeling emotionally flat or having trouble speaking.
Aside from these strong beliefs, have you ever heard voices when no one is around, or seen things that others cannot see?
No, I've never heard any voices or seen things that others can't see. My concerns are entirely based on what I have actually observed happening with the lab orders and patients at my clinic.

Do you believe that these labs are using technology or methods that are physically impossible or beyond the realm of reality, or are your concerns based on events that could theoretically happen in the real world?

No, this isn't sci-fi or impossible technology at all; it's entirely based on real-world events. As a phlebotomist, I see routine lab orders, patient names, and referrals every day, which makes this a very plausible ethical concern. It is just a coordinated program happening right under our noses using standard clinical procedures.
Have you ever felt that you have special powers, or that you are being followed or monitored by these groups in a way that is specifically targeted at you personally?

I don't have any special powers, and I don't think anyone is following me around on the street. However, I definitely feel monitored at work, especially since certain coworkers always glance at each other whenever I walk by. It is clear to me that they are keeping tabs on me because I am paying attention to the research program targeting our community.

Do you believe that these coworkers are actively conspiring to harm you or prevent you from exposing the program, or do you feel they are simply observing you because they are aware of your suspicions?

I'm not sure if they want to physically harm me, but their constant glances make me feel very watched and uncomfortable. I believe they are monitoring me because they are either involved in the cover-up or realize I'm onto the program. I've been avoiding them because I don't trust them and feel they are trying to keep the secret safe.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a persistent, non-bizarre persecutory delusion regarding a conspiracy at their workplace, lasting over one year. There is a clear absence of hallucinations, disorganized speech, negative symptoms, or significant functional impairment, ruling out schizophrenia. The belief system is encapsulated and does not impact their ability to perform their job, which is characteristic of delusional disorder.
